# docker_networks (Data Source)

Lists the networks on the provider's Docker host (`GET /networks`), like `docker network ls`. The optional arguments are Engine API filters; the list is sorted by name, then ID.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Every user-defined bridge network carrying the label team=web.
data "docker_networks" "web" {
  driver = "bridge"
  type   = "custom"
  labels = { team = "web" }
}

output "web_network_names" {
  value = data.docker_networks.web.names
}

# Subnets of the first match, from the structured list.
output "first_network_subnets" {
  value = try([for c in data.docker_networks.web.networks[0].ipam.config : c.subnet], [])
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `dangling` (Boolean) `true` lists only networks no container uses, `false` only used ones.
- `driver` (String) Only networks using this driver, e.g. `bridge` or `overlay`.
- `id` (String) Only networks whose ID starts with this value (Engine `id` filter).
- `labels` (Map of String) Only networks carrying every one of these labels (Engine `label` filter); an empty value matches any value.
- `name` (String) Only networks whose name matches (Engine `name` filter, a substring match).
- `scope` (String) Only networks of this scope: `local`, `swarm` or `global`.
- `type` (String) `custom` lists only user-defined networks, `builtin` only the predefined `bridge`, `host` and `none`.

### Read-Only

- `content_sha256` (String) sha256 of networks_json.
- `docker_server_version` (String) Docker Engine version from GET /version.
- `engine_api_version` (String) Engine API version negotiated with the daemon (min of the client maximum and GET /version ApiVersion).
- `ids` (List of String) IDs of the listed networks, in the order of `networks`.
- `names` (List of String) Names of the listed networks, in the order of `networks`.
- `networks` (Attributes List) The GET /networks response as a nested object, field by field. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--networks))
- `networks_json` (String) The Engine API GET /networks response as JSON; entries sorted by name, then ID. Re-encoded, not byte-exact: the moby client keeps no raw body for this call, so this is the decoded response written as canonical JSON (keys sorted, compact).
